subject.title: fix(gateway/ui): split session group mutations to avoid concurrent add loss

question: Should `sessions.groups.reorder` become a supported public Gateway contract now despite the absence of a production reorder caller?
rationale: Publishing the method affects protocol, Android, server, and UI compatibility surfaces; whether that capability should exist cannot be decided solely from the concurrent-add bug report.

options.title: Keep add only
options.body: Remove the reorder method and related exports, Android enum entry, UI capability, tests, and mocks; this leaves the focused atomic-add regression fix.

options.title: Adopt reorder deliberately
options.body: Wire a real production reorder flow to the method and document stable ordering, old-client behavior, and the intended long-term contract.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Hold the change until maintainers choose the durable session-group mutation API shape.

recommendation.title: Keep add only
recommendation.body: Remove the reorder method and related exports, Android enum entry, UI capability, tests, and mocks; this leaves the focused atomic-add regression fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the linked reproduction and explicitly identified semantic Gateway mutations as the relevant fix boundary, though source-history ownership was not available in this review.
